griego: βαπτισμῶν διδαχὴν, ἐπιθέσεώς τε χειρῶν, ἀναστάσεώς τε νεκρῶν, καὶ κρίματος αἰωνίου

text_src: The ⸢powers⸣ could refer to: (1) what God will do, sometimes through other people, for those who believe. («what God will do powerfully in the age to come»); (2) how people can do “powerful” things. («the powerful things that people will do in the age to come»)

text_src: The phrase ⸢for themselves⸣ could mean that: (1) they are acting to benefit themselves only. («since they are crucifying again for their own benefit»); (2) they do these things ⸢themselves⸣. («since they themselves are crucifying again»)
The phrase ⸢Son of God⸣ is an important title for Jesus that describes his relationship to God the Father.
The phrase ⸢useful vegetation⸣ refers to plants that grow on the ⸢land⸣ and that benefit people. They could be plants that people eat, or they could be plants that people use for other purposes.

griego: ἐπεὶ κατ’ οὐδενὸς εἶχεν μείζονος ὀμόσαι, ὤμοσεν καθ’ ἑαυτοῦ

text_src: In the author’s culture, people often ⸢swore by⸣ someone else. griego: πάσης αὐτοῖς ἀντιλογίας πέρας, εἰς βεβαίωσιν ὁ ὅρκος

text_src: The author uses technical language related to ⸢disputes⸣ and the law courts. The word ⸢end⸣ refers to a final decision, while the word ⸢confirmation⸣ refers to how something is backed up and proved to be true by evidence or, here, an ⸢oath⸣.

text_src: The author does not specify from what ⸢we⸣ have ⸢fled⸣ or who provides the ⸢refuge⸣. He implies that God provides the ⸢refuge⸣, but from what ⸢we⸣ have ⸢fled⸣ is not clear. An ⸢anchor⸣ is a heavy piece of metal attached to the end of a rope. The other end of the rope is tied to a boat, and in this way, when it is dropped down to the land under the water, the anchor keeps the boat from moving around or drifting away.

text_src: The phrase ⸢on our behalf⸣ could modify: (1) ⸢entered⸣. In this case, Jesus has ⸢entered⸣ for our sake, or to help us. («has entered for our sake as a forerunner»); (2) ⸢forerunner⸣. In this case, Jesus opened the way ⸢on our behalf⸣. («has entered as a forerunner who leads us»)

text_src: The phrases ⸢holy place⸣ and ⸢true tabernacle⸣ could describe: (1) the inner room of the sanctuary (⸢holy place⸣) and the entire sanctuary (⸢true tabernacle⸣). griego: ὄντων τῶν προσφερόντων κατὰ νόμον τὰ δῶρα

text_src: The author refers to how God revealed to Moses what the ⸢tabernacle⸣, the sanctuary that the Israelites used when they were in the desert, should be like. Moses then told the Israelites how to ⸢complete the tabernacle⸣.

griego: διαφορωτέρας … λειτουργίας … κρείττονός … διαθήκης … κρείττοσιν ἐπαγγελίαις
